Lesson 4: Momentum and Energy

jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:36:42 t V
If there's some sort of outside force on a system, its momentum isn't conserved. For example, if you stand up and start walking, you'll pick up some momentum in the direction that you're walking. Your momentum wasn't conserved.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:36:56 t V
Momentum is still conserved overall. If we define a bigger system, consisting of you plus the entire Earth, then momentum is conserved. You pick up forward momentum as you start walking and the Earth picks up backward momentum to cancel it, but because the Earth is so big, its velocity due to this momentum change is negligible, and considering momentum conservation doesn't really buy us any understanding of the situation. So we need to make sure we define systems carefully today.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:37:30 t V
As we know, Fnet=ΔpΔtFnet=ΔpΔt
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:38:16 t V
But if Fnet=0Fnet=0 then the change in momentum must be zero as well ⟶⟶ conserved.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:38:48 t V
This is how Newton formulated his original second law (not F=maF=ma).
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:39:16 t V
Although he called momentum "quantity of motion".

Next, let's look at a problem from the 2014 F=ma exam.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 19:55:12 t V
A cubical box of mass 10kg10kg with edge length 5m5m is free to move on a frictionless horizontal surface. Inside is a small block of mass 2kg,2kg, which moves without friction inside the box. At time t=0,t=0, the block is moving with velocity 5m/s5m/s directly towards one of the faces of the box, while the box is initially at rest. The coefficient of restitution for any collision between the block and box is 90%, meaning that the relative speed between the box and block immediately after a collision is 90% of the relative speed between the box and block immediately before the collision. After 1 minute, the block is a displacement xx from the original position. Which of the following is closest to x?x?

Good. This is a useful tool. This reference frame, the center of mass, is a very common way to solve problems.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 20:17:42 t V
Any system that conserves momentum has constant momentum. So, since the system must also have constant mass, any system that conserves momentum has a center of mass that moves at a constant velocity. The individual pieces of the system might be doing all sorts of crazy things, but when we calculate the location of the center of mass, it's simply moving along in perfect linear motion in a straight line at constant speed.

jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:26 t V
Summary
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:29 t V
One of the most important steps in solving a problem is to develop a plan.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:31 t V
Sometimes, before we can map out a plan, we need to explore the problem a bit, making sure we understand what it's asking and what the important principles involved in the problem are.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:33 t V
Momentum and energy are the two most important conserved quantities in mechanics.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:36 t V
Momentum is conserved whenever there are no outside forces on a system.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:38 t V
Mechanical energy may or may not be conserved, even if there are no outside forces. It's when there is no dissipation (such as friction or inelastic collisions) and no input (like chemical energy from muscles or train engines) that mechanical energy is conserved.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:43 t V
Momentum, force, and time are related. The rate of change of a system's momentum is equal to the external force on it. Consequently, the momentum gained by a system can be calculated via the area under a graph of the net force on the system over time.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:47 t V
Energy, force, and displacement are related as well. The total change in energy of a system is equal to the area under a force versus displacement graph.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:50 t V
The power delivered to a system by a force is P=→F⋅→v.P=F→⋅v→.
jonjoseph 2025-07-02 21:07:55 t V
There are usually several ways to solve an F=ma problem. Making a plan allows us to pick one path. If that path turns out not to work very well, we can still switch to another one.

On September 17, 1787, thirty-nine delegates signed the Constitution in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, establishing the United States of America. The Founding Fathers had created a representative government where all its citizens could express their voices. Americans had little representation in Parliament when it was a British colony, which led the Founding Fathers to ensure that everyone had a voice in the new country. How are our voices important?
